transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... I just keep making myself throw up after I eat. I've been doing it a lot in the bathroom at work, actually. I work at a dry cleaner's over on Elm, and honestly, the bathroom there is tiny and it always smells like those harsh chemicals. We have this one pressing machine that's been broken for like three weeks, and my boss Gary refuses to call the repair guy, so it just pumps heat into the whole shop. It gets so unbelievably hot, and I'm on my feet all day dealing with people's heavy coats and dirty shirts, you know? 

But, yeah, I'll go in that little bathroom, or right when I get home, and just... make myself throw up. I really hate it. I do. But it's just started feeling like the only way I can actually calm down. My sister keeps telling me I should try yoga or something to relax, but who has the money for that? Plus, my knees are completely shot from standing on concrete all day anyway, so I don't think I could even do those poses... but, yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.
Can you describe what typically happens before you make yourself throw up? Do you usually feel like you've eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Um, yeah, I guess I do. It's like... when it happens, I can go through a full bag of chips, a bunch of pastries from the corner store, whatever leftovers I can find, and a bunch of sweet drinks all in one sitting. I do it so fast I don't even really notice how much is gone until I'm looking at all the empty wrappers. 

I usually get the pastries from Tony's deli, which is just down the block from the dry cleaners. Tony's a nice enough guy, but I swear he marks up the prices on those little powdered donuts every single week. I was in there on Tuesday and he was just screaming at his delivery driver about parking in the alley, holding up the entire line at the register. I just wanted to pay for my stuff and get out of there, you know? The alley behind our shop is a total nightmare anyway, the garbage trucks can barely fit back there because of how the bins are set up. Gary keeps saying he's gonna call the city to complain about the dumpsters taking up too much space, but Gary never actually does anything he says he will. Just like with the broken pressing machine, he just talks and talks. 

Um... wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the food. But yeah, I just eat a ton of it really fast before I go to the bathroom.
During these episodes when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yeah, I do. It's exactly like that. Once I start, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for food even while I'm screaming at myself in my head to stop. It's like I'm just watching myself do it and I can't make myself quit. It's so weird, like my brain just disconnects from my body. 

Speaking of disconnecting, my TV cable has been acting up all week, just completely cutting out right in the middle of my shows. I called the cable company and they kept me on hold for an hour and forty-five minutes. Can you believe that? And the music they play while you're waiting is just this awful, repetitive elevator music that makes you want to pull your hair out. The guy finally answers and tells me there's an outage in my area, but my neighbor Mrs. Higgins—she lives right across the hall, the one with the three yappy little Pomeranians that never shut up—she said her cable is working just fine. She was watching some home shopping network channel and bought this ridiculous gold-plated vegetable peeler. Who needs a gold-plated vegetable peeler? I just use this old rusty one I've had since I moved into that apartment ten years ago. It barely works, honestly, I should probably throw it out before I give myself tetanus or something. 

But, um, yeah. I just can't stop once I start eating. It's completely out of my hands.
How often do you make yourself throw up after these eating episodes, and do you feel like you do it to try to control your weight or keep from gaining weight?

Well, for months now, I'd say most weeks have at least a couple of those episodes... where I eat way too much and then try to undo it, you know? Usually by throwing up, but sometimes I just try not to eat at all the next day, or I try to walk it off. Though walking is tough because, like I said, my knees are just completely ruined. 

I actually tried to buy some new shoes for work, those ones with the thick foam soles that nurses wear? I saw an ad for them on my phone while I was sitting on the bus. The bus system here is just getting worse and worse, by the way. I waited forty minutes in the freezing rain on Thursday because the 42 bus just never showed up. And when the next one finally came, the heater was broken and the driver was playing this terrible country music so loud I couldn't even hear myself think. There was this guy sitting across from me eating a tuna sandwich at seven in the morning. Who eats tuna on a crowded bus at dawn? It smelled awful, almost as bad as the chemicals at the shop. I had to crack the window, which just let more freezing rain in, so my coat was soaked by the time I got to Gary's. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, the weight thing. Yeah, I mean, I definitely do it because I'm terrified of gaining weight. If I didn't get rid of it, I'd be huge, and I just... I can't handle that. So yeah, at least a couple times a week for a few months now.
Do you regularly use behaviors like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain after eating large amounts of food?

Well, yeah, like I said, I throw up. But also, on the days after I eat too much, I try to make up for it by not eating anything until really late in the day. Or I'll try to walk and exercise a bunch, even when my legs are just throbbing from standing at the dry cleaners all day. 

Standing on that concrete floor is brutal, honestly. Gary refuses to buy those anti-fatigue mats. He says they're a tripping hazard, but I know it's just because he doesn't want to spend the money. He's so cheap. Last week, he tried to fix the leaky pipe in the employee bathroom with duct tape instead of calling a plumber. Of course, it burst over the weekend, and when we came in on Monday, there was an inch of water on the floor. It smelled like mildew for three days, and my favorite pair of sneakers got completely ruined because I had to wade through it to get to the mop bucket. I tried to clean it up, but the mop head was so old and gross it probably just made things worse. I told him we needed a new mop like a month ago, but he just ignores me. 

But, um, anyway, yeah. I try not to eat the next day, or I force myself to exercise even when I'm exhausted and my legs hurt, just to try to undo all the food.
